html:
The Goshute are a Western Shoshone people of the Great Salt Lake Desert, on today's border of Utah and Nevada. They are close kin of the Western Shoshone and neighbours of the Southern Paiute and the Utes.

Their land was one of the driest parts of the Great Basin. They lived in small family groups, moving with the seasons to gather seeds, roots and pine nuts, and hunting rabbits in communal drives. They also ate insects, which led later settlers to look down on them.

Mormon settlers arrived from 1847, and the Pony Express and stage lines crossed Goshute land around 1860, bringing conflict over water and grass. Today there are two Goshute tribes: the Confederated Tribes of the Goshute Reservation on the state line and the Skull Valley Band in Utah. See also Eastern Shoshone.
